claim: Mammalian heart development requires precise allocation of cardiac progenitors.
source: Mammalian heart development requires precise allocation of cardiac progenitors.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by the overall findings of the study.

claim: The existence of a multipotent progenitor for all anatomic and cellular components of the heart has been predicted but its identity and contribution to the two cardiac progenitor 'fields' has remained undefined.
source: The existence of a multipotent progenitor for all anatomic and cellular components of the heart has been predicted but its identity and contribution to the two cardiac progenitor 'fields' has remained undefined.
evidence: This statement references prior predictions in the field and identifies a knowledge gap, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Mesp1+ cells in gastrulating mesoderm are rapidly specified into committed cardiac precursors fated for distinct anatomic regions of the heart.
source: Here we show, using clonal genetic fate mapping, that Mesp1+ cells in gastrulating mesoderm are rapidly specified into committed cardiac precursors fated for distinct anatomic regions of the heart.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by clonal MADM analysis data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Smarcd3 is a marker of early specified cardiac precursors.
source: We identify Smarcd3 as a marker of early specified cardiac precursors
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data (Figure 3), lineage tracing experiments (Figure 5), and ES cell differentiation data (Figure 6).

claim: A compartment boundary exists at the future junction of the left and right ventricles that arises prior to morphogenesis.
source: identify within these precursors a compartment boundary at the future junction of the left and right ventricles that arises prior to morphogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by clonal analysis showing sharp boundaries in the IVS (Figure 7A-D) and lineage tracing of Tbx5 and Mef2cAHF populations (Figure 7E-P).

claim: The cellular and anatomical fate of mesoderm-derived cardiac cells is specified very early.
source: Our studies define the timing and hierarchy of cardiac progenitor specification and demonstrate that the cellular and anatomical fate of mesoderm-derived cardiac cells is specified very early.
evidence: This conclusion is supported by the clonal analysis and lineage tracing experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: At least two sets of molecularly and morphologically distinct cardiac precursors have been identified in the mammalian embryo, referred to as the first and second heart fields.
source: At least two sets of molecularly and morphologically distinct cardiac precursors have been identified in the mammalian embryo, referred to as the first and second heart fields; these populations contribute to distinct anatomical structures within the heart (Evans et al., 2010; Buckingham et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The interventricular septum myocardium has a dual contribution from the first and second heart fields.
source: it has been postulated that the IVS myocardium has a dual contribution from these two heart fields (Bruneau et al., 1999; Takeuchi et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a postulation from prior literature, supported by citations.

claim: A population of early mesoderm expressing Mesp1 precedes the establishment of the anatomically and molecularly distinct 'heart fields'.
source: Previous studies have suggested that a population of early mesoderm expressing the transcription factor Mesp1 precedes the establishment of the anatomically and molecularly distinct 'heart fields' (Saga et al., 1996, 1999; Bondue et al., 2008; Lindsley et al., 2008)
evidence: This is based on previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: Mesp1+ cells can contribute to a broad range of mesodermal derivatives that include, but are not restricted to, the developing heart.
source: However it is clear that Mesp1+ cells can also contribute to a broad range of mesodermal derivatives that include, but are not restricted to, the developing heart (Chan et al., 2013; Yoshida et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations and confirmed by the authors' own lineage tracing data in Figure 1A.

claim: Mesp1+ cells contribute broadly to several mesodermal derivatives.
source: In reassessing the in vivo differentiation potential of Mesp1+ cells, we find that this population contributes broadly to several mesodermal derivatives, (Figure 1A), consistent with other reports (Yoshida et al., 2008).
evidence: This is directly shown in Figure 1A and supported by citation.

claim: Among the diverse Mesp1+ mesodermal population, a more specific population destined for the cardiac lineage exists.
source: We reasoned that among this diverse mesodermal population, a more specific population destined for the cardiac lineage exists.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that is subsequently tested and supported by the clonal analysis data.

claim: Mesp1Cre is active in mesoderm from approximately E6.0 to E7.5.
source: clones induced by Mesp1Cre (which is active in mesoderm from ∼E6.0 to E7.5) (Saga et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation and confirmed by in situ hybridization in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: By the late head fold stage, Mesp1Cre mRNA is downregulated and localized to the base of the allantois with no expression in the area of forming cardiogenic mesoderm.
source: By the late head fold stage (LHF), we see a downregulation of Cre mRNA and localization to the base of the allantois. We see no expression in the area of forming cardiogenic mesoderm.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: No additional recombination events occurred between E8.5 and E14.5 in Mesp1Cre-MADM embryos.
source: In addition, we counted the number of labeling events in embryos at E8.5 and E14.5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–E and Statistical Analysis) and saw no change in the distribution of labeled clusters, suggesting that no additional recombination events have occurred over this time interval.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: A subset of clones uniquely label the heart, demonstrating the existence of an early, cardiac-specific progenitor.
source: A subset of clones uniquely label the heart (Figure 1D–E and Figure 2), demonstrating the existence of an early, cardiac-specific progenitor.
evidence: This is directly shown in Figures 1D-E and Figure 2.

claim: Specimens with clones of cells in other mesodermal derivatives but with no apparent clones within the heart were found.
source: We also found specimens with clones of cells in other mesodermal derivatives but with no apparent clones within the heart (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–G and Figure 2)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F-G and documented in Figure 2.

claim: Within the Mesp1+ population, a dedicated population of cardiac progenitors exists.
source: conclusively demonstrating that within the population of Mesp1+ mesoderm a dedicated population of cardiac progenitors exists.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the observation of heart-specific clones and non-cardiac clones from the same Mesp1+ population.

claim: Mesp1Cre-MADM twin spots did not populate anatomic structures classically thought to derive from both first and second heart field progenitors.
source: In contrast to previous retrospective clonal analysis (Meilhac et al., 2004b), we did not observe twin spots that populated anatomic structures classically thought to derive from first and second heart field progenitors, for example spanning the left and right ventricles, or contributing to the left ventricle and outflow tract.
evidence: This is based on the absence of such clones in the data presented in Figure 2 and throughout the manuscript.

claim: Twin spots populated discrete anatomic locations including the left ventricle, right ventricle, outflow tract, atria-left ventricle, and interventricular septum.
source: Rather, we saw twin spots that populated discreet anatomic locations including the left ventricle (Figure 1F–G and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B), right ventricle (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–D), outflow tract (Figure 1N–O and Figure 1—figure supplement 3E–F), atria-left ventricle (Figure 1L–M), and interventricular septum (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is directly shown in the cited figures.

claim: Twin spots that spanned the right and left ventricles were notably absent from the clonal analysis.
source: Notably absent from our clonal analysis were twin spots that spanned the right and left ventricles.
evidence: This is based on the comprehensive documentation of all clones in Figure 2.

claim: Based on 96 clonal observations, the probability that a common progenitor for the left and right ventricles does not exist is high (upper limit of 95% confidence interval is 0.019).
source: Based on the total number of clonal observations made (n = 96), the probability that a common progenitor for the left and right ventricles does not exist, assuming a binomial distribution (success, or 1, = the progenitor is observed; failure, or 0 = the progenitor is not observed), can be calculated using Jeffreys interval. The upper and lower limits of a 95% confidence interval was calculated such that the upper limit is 0.019 (See Statistical Methods).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the clonal data.

claim: The discrepancy between Mesp1Cre-MADM clonal analysis and prior retrospective clonal analyses lies with the timing of the labeling events.
source: An explanation for the discrepancy between our Mesp1Cre-MADM clonal analysis and prior retrospective clonal analyses lies with the timing of the labeling events.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparing the current results with previous studies.

claim: Mesp1 is transiently expressed, so all clones are induced over a narrow window of time during gastrulation.
source: Mesp1 is transiently expressed ((Saga et al., 1999) and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), thus all of our clones are induced over a narrow window of time during gastrulation.
evidence: This is supported by citation and in situ hybridization data.

claim: Shortly after a heart field progenitor is specified, the anatomic destiny of daughter cells quickly diverge, especially those destined to occupy the left or right ventricle, and these fates remain fixed.
source: In summary, our results suggest that soon after a heart field progenitor is specified, shortly after the initiation of gastrulation, the anatomic destiny of daughter cells quickly diverge, especially those destined to occupy /contribute to the left or right ventricle, and these fates remain fixed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the clonal analysis data.

claim: Most twin spots give rise to homogenous cellular progeny (cardiomyocytes or endothelial cells).
source: In analyzing the cellular composition of Mesp1Cre-MADM clones, we noticed that while most twin spots give rise to homogenous cellular progeny (cardiomyocytes or endothelial cells)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cellular composition of clones shown in various figures.

claim: Individual cardiac progenitors (<5%) can contribute to multiple cell types, for example myocardium and endocardium, or endothelium and smooth muscle.
source: individual cardiac progenitors (<5%, see Figure 2) can contribute to multiple cell types, for example myocardium and endocardium (Figure 1J–K and Figure 1—figure supplement 3J–L), or endothelium and smooth muscle (Figure 1O).
evidence: This is shown in the cited figures and quantified in Figure 2.

claim: A multipotent progenitor had been predicted from in vitro ES cell-based differentiation models.
source: While a multipotent progenitor had been predicted from in vitro ES cell-based differentiation models (Wu et al., 2006; Moretti et al., 2006)
evidence: This is based on citations to previous studies.

claim: This is the first evidence of the existence of a multipotent progenitor in vivo.
source: this is the first evidence of the existence of such a multipotent progenitor in vivo.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding, based on the data showing multipotent clones.

claim: Smarcd3 expression precedes Isl1 and Tbx5 in a domain at the anterior-proximal region of the embryo extending into extraembryonic tissues.
source: We find that Smarcd3 expression precedes Isl1 and Tbx5 in a domain that lies at the anterior-proximal region of the embryo and extends into the extraembryonic tissues (Figure 3B,D–E).
evidence: This is shown by in situ hybridization in Figure 3.

claim: Smarcd3 expression domain appears coincident temporally but non-overlapping with Mesp1 expression.
source: This expression domain appears coincident temporally but non-overlapping with Mesp1 expression (Figure 3A–B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is shown by in situ hybridization in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Smarcd3 expression is within the Mesp1Cre-derived lineage.
source: but is within the Mesp1Cre-derived lineage (Figure 4O–P).
evidence: This is shown by lineage tracing in Figure 4O-P.

claim: Activity of the Mef2cAHF enhancer is detected at the late streak stage prior to the expression of Tbx5 and Isl1.
source: Activity of the Mef2cAHF enhancer (Verzi et al., 2005) is also detected at the LS stage (Figure 3C) prior to the expression of Tbx5 and Isl1.
evidence: This is shown by lacZ staining in Figure 3C.

claim: Activity of the Mef2cAHF enhancer is dependent on Isl1.
source: Previous studies have shown that activity of this enhancer is dependent on Isl1 (Dodou et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on a citation to a previous study.

claim: No detectable Isl1 reporter activity was seen in late streak stage embryos.
source: While there was robust ß-galactosidase reporter activity at the cardiac crescent stage, no detectable staining was seen in LS stage embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–B)
evidence: This is shown by lacZ staining in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Initiation of Mef2cAHF enhancer expression precedes Isl1 expression and its initiation may be independent of Isl1.
source: suggesting that initiation of Mef2cAHF enhancer expression precedes Isl1 expression and its initiation may be independent of Isl1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal expression data.

claim: At the early head fold stage, weak Isl1 and Tbx5 expression is detectable, Mef2cAHF activity remains, and Smarcd3 expression restricts to the embryo proper.
source: Several hours later (EHF stage), weak Isl1 and Tbx5 expression is detectable, Mef2cAHF activity remains, and Smarcd3 expression restricts to the embryo proper (Figure 3G–J).
evidence: This is shown by in situ hybridization and lacZ staining in Figure 3G-J.

claim: Flk1 labels multipotent progenitors that can differentiate into hematopoietic, endothelial, smooth muscle and cardiac lineages.
source: The VEGF-A receptor Flk1 labels multipotent progenitors that can differentiate into hematopoietic, endothelial, smooth muscle and cardiac lineages (Ishitobi et al., 2011; Kattman et al., 2006)
evidence: This is based on citations to previous studies.

claim: There is minimal overlap between Mesp1 and Flk1 in late streak embryos.
source: While we find minimal overlap between Mesp1 and Flk1 and Mesp1 and a reporter of early Smarcd3 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,C–D)
evidence: This is shown by co-staining in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There is significant overlap of Flk1 with a reporter of early Smarcd3 expression in late streak stage embryos.
source: there is significant overlap of Flk1 with this same reporter of early Smarcd3 expression (see below) in late streak stage embryos.
evidence: This is shown by co-staining in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There is an orderly progression of gene expression that follows the progressive commitment of nascent mesoderm, from early expression of Mesp1 to intermediate expression of Smarcd3, Flk1, and the Mef2cAHF enhancer, and finally later cardiac lineage-specific expression of Tbx5 and Isl1.
source: Taken together, we see an orderly progression of gene expression that follows the progressive commitment of nascent mesoderm, from early expression of Mesp1 to the intermediate expression of Smarcd3, Flk1, and the Mef2cAHF enhancer, and finally the later cardiac lineage-specific expression of Tbx5 and Isl1 (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is a summary of the temporal expression data shown in Figure 3.

claim: An approximately 9 kb genomic element (Smarcd3-F1) is sufficient to recapitulate early endogenous Smarcd3 expression.
source: We tested an ∼9 kb genomic element we called Smarcd3-F1 in a transgenic mouse reporter assay and found that it was sufficient to recapitulate early endogenous Smarcd3 expression (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is shown by reporter expression in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Smarcd3-F1 expression was maintained in the cardiac crescent and looping heart at later stages of development.
source: Expression was maintained in the cardiac crescent and looping heart at later stages of development (Figure 4E–I)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4E-I.

claim: An approximately 2.5 kb genomic element (Smarcd3-F6) is expressed only in the embryo proper, in a more restricted pattern than Smarcd3-F1.
source: Through deletion analysis of the 9 kb enhancer/promoter region (Smarcd3-F1), we defined an ∼2.5 kb genomic element (Smarcd3-F6) that is expressed only in the embryo proper, in a more restricted pattern than Smarcd3-F1 (Figure 4D and J–N and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by reporter expression in Figure 4D and J-N.

claim: Lineage labeling of Smarcd3-F1CreERT2; RosaR26R at E5.5 and observation at E10.5 marked cells that contribute predominantly to the heart and anterior forelimb, with scattered cells in the trunk and cranial mesoderm.
source: Lineage labeling of Smarcd3-F1CreERT2; RosaR26R at E5.5 and observation at E10.5 marked cells that contribute predominantly to the heart and anterior forelimb (Figure 5A–B), with scattered cells in the trunk and cranial mesoderm (Figure 5A and data not shown)
evidence: This is shown by lineage tracing in Figure 5A-B.

claim: Within the heart, Smarcd3-F1+ labeled cells contribute to cardiomyocyte, endocardial, and pericardial layers.
source: Within the heart, labeled cells contribute to cardiomyocyte, endocardial, and pericardial layers (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Lineage tracing with Smarcd3-F6CreERT2 labeled a much smaller number of more spatially defined cells, including the heart and a small group of cells in the anterior forelimb.
source: Indeed, lineage tracing with Smarcd3-F6CreERT2 labeled a much smaller number of more spatially defined cells, including the heart and a small group of cells in the anterior forelimb (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: This is shown by lineage tracing in Figure 5D-E.

claim: There was minimal to no labeling in head/trunk mesoderm or in extraembryonic tissues with Smarcd3-F6CreERT2.
source: There was minimal to no labeling in head/trunk mesoderm or in extraembryonic tissues
evidence: This is based on the lineage tracing data shown in Figure 5D-E and Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-C.

claim: Within the heart, Smarcd3-F6CreERT2 labeled primarily the myocardial layer.
source: and within the heart Smarcd3-F6CreERT2 labeled primarily the myocardial layer (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 3A–C)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-C.

claim: Smarcd3-F6 enhancer labels a more restricted population of cells than Smarcd3-F1.
source: consistent with this enhancer labeling a more restricted population of cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparing the lineage tracing results of F1 and F6.

claim: Smarcd3 expression in the late gastrulating embryo labels a defined population of specified cardiac precursors that are fated to occupy unique anatomic structures within the mature heart.
source: We conclude that Smarcd3 expression in the late gastrulating embryo labels a defined population of specified cardiac precursors that are fated to occupy unique anatomic structures within the mature heart.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lineage tracing and clonal analysis data.

claim: Expression of Mesp1 is rapidly induced at early mesoderm stage (Day 3-Day 4) in ES cell differentiation.
source: In this system, we find expression of Mesp1 is rapidly induced at early mesoderm stage (Day 3-Day 4) while expression of the cardiac precursor markers Nkx2-5 and Tbx5 initiate about a day later (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is shown by qPCR data in Figure 6C.

claim: Expression of Smarcd3 and the Smarcd3-F6 reporter are detectable in ES cells and gradually decline until both are sharply induced at Day 4.
source: Expression of Smarcd3 as well as the Smarcd3-F6 reporter are detectable in ES cells and gradually decline until both are sharply induced at Day 4.
evidence: This is shown by qPCR data in Figure 6B.

claim: At Day 4, Mesp1 expression is rapidly downregulated.
source: At the same time, Mesp1 expression is rapidly downregulated (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is shown by qPCR data in Figure 6B.

claim: Mesp1 and Smarcd3 mRNA are largely non-overlapping, temporally, in ES cell differentiation.
source: As a result, Mesp1 and Smarcd3 mRNA are largely non-overlapping, temporally.
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal expression data in Figure 6B-C.

claim: GFP+ cells from Smarcd3-F6 reporter ES cells expressed genes associated with early cardiovascular progenitors (e.g. Hand2, Gata4, and Meis1).
source: GFP + cells expressed genes associated with early cardiovascular progenitors (e.g. Hand2, Gata4, and Meis1), while GFP- cells expressed genes associated with hematopoietic and other lineages.
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq data in Figure 6D.

claim: GFP- cells from Smarcd3-F6 reporter ES cells expressed genes associated with hematopoietic and other lineages.
source: GFP + cells expressed genes associated with early cardiovascular progenitors (e.g. Hand2, Gata4, and Meis1), while GFP- cells expressed genes associated with hematopoietic and other lineages.
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq data in Figure 6D.

claim: Tal1/Scl appears to be depleted in the GFP+ population/enriched in the GFP- population from Smarcd3-F6 reporter ES cells.
source: One gene of interest that appears to be depleted in our GFP + population/enriched in our GFP- population is Tal1/Scl.
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Tal1/Scl has been implicated as a critical component of endocardial morphogenesis.
source: This gene had been implicated as a critical component of endocardial morphogenesis (Bussmann et al., 2007)
evidence: This is based on a citation to a previous study.

claim: Tal1/Scl has been shown to repress cardiomyogenesis in yolk sac vasculature and endocardium.
source: and more recently has been shown to repress cardiomyogenesis in yolk sac vasculature and endocardium (Van Handel et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on a citation to a previous study.

claim: Cells labeled by the Smarcd3-F6 enhancer, both in vivo and in vitro, represent an early cardiac progenitor population.
source: Overall, these results indicate that cells labeled by the Smarcd3-F6 enhancer, both in vivo and in vitro, represent an early cardiac progenitor population.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lineage tracing and RNA-seq data.

claim: Twin spots within the interventricular septum formed a sharp boundary, reminiscent of compartment boundaries classically defined in the Drosophila wing imaginal disc and mammalian midbrain-hindbrain boundary.
source: These twin spots formed a sharp boundary within the IVS, reminiscent of compartment boundaries classically defined in the Drosophila wing imaginal disc and mammalian midbrain-hindbrain boundary (Lawrence and Struhl, 1996; Dahmann and Basler, 1999).
evidence: This is based on observation of clones in Figure 7A-D and comparison to known compartment boundaries.

claim: The Mef2c-AHF enhancer is expressed very early in the embryo, in a domain that appeared to partially overlap with that of Smarcd3.
source: We found that this enhancer element is expressed very early in the embryo, in a domain that appeared to partially overlap with that of Smarcd3 (Figure 3C,H).
evidence: This is shown by lacZ staining in Figure 3C and H.

claim: Endothelial and myocardial components of the outflow tract, right ventricle, and IVS are derived from the Mef2cAHF enhancer population.
source: Previous work using a constitutive Cre recombinase expressed under the control of the Mef2cAHF enhancer suggested that endothelial and myocardial components of the outflow tract, right ventricle, and IVS are derived from this population (Verzi et al., 2005).
evidence: This is based on a citation to a previous study.

claim: In the looped heart, expression of Tbx5 is restricted to the left ventricle and atria with very little expression in the right ventricle or outflow tract.
source: In the looped heart, expression of Tbx5 is restricted to the left ventricle and atria with very little expression in the right ventricle or outflow tract (Bruneau et al., 1999).
evidence: This is based on a citation to a previous study.

claim: Early labeling of Tbx5+ cells marked cells that were predominantly restricted to the left ventricle and atria.
source: Early labeling of Tbx5+ cells marked cells that were predominantly restricted to the left ventricle and atria (Figure 7E–F and 7I–L)
evidence: This is shown by lineage tracing in Figure 7E-F and 7I-L.

claim: Scattered surface labeling on the right ventricle was seen with early tamoxifen injection in Tbx5CreERT2 mice, but myocardial labeling was limited to the LV up to the junction with the RV at the IVS.
source: scattered surface labeling on the right ventricle (Figure 7—figure supplement 1I–J) was also seen with early tamoxifen injection, but myocardial labeling was limited to the LV up to the junction with the RV at the IVS.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1I-J.

claim: Earlier observation at E8.5 following a pulse of tamoxifen at E6.5 in Tbx5CreERT2 mice revealed labeling in a restricted population of cells within the presumptive left ventricle.
source: Earlier observation at E8.5 following a pulse of tamoxifen at E6.5 revealed labeling in a restricted population of cells within the presumptive left ventricle (Figure 7—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Tbx5 lineage restriction arises early and is not a consequence of later sorting out of cells.
source: suggesting that the Tbx5 lineage restriction arises early and is not a consequence of later sorting out of cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the early labeling data in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Labeling Mef2cAHF+ cells at E6.5 marked a complementary population of cells that were largely restricted to the right ventricle and outflow tract.
source: Labeling Mef2cAHF + cells at E6.5 marked a complementary population of cells that were largely restricted to the right ventricle and outflow tract (Figure 7G–H and Figure 7—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is shown by lineage tracing in Figure 7G-H and Figure 7—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Early Mef2cAHF+ cells are within the Smarcd3-F1 lineage.
source: Using an intersectional reporter that responds to the combined activity of Cre and Dre we confirmed that these early Mef2cAHF + cells are also within the Smarcd3-F1 lineage (Figure 7M and Figure 7—figure supplement 3B–C).
evidence: This is shown by intersectional lineage tracing in Figure 7M and Figure 7—figure supplement 3B-C.

claim: The expression of Tbx5 and the Mef2AHF enhancer labels complementary populations that are established prior to morphogenesis, which correspond, in part, to left and right ventricular precursors, respectively.
source: The expression of Tbx5 and the Mef2AHF enhancer appears to label complementary populations that are established prior to morphogenesis, which correspond, in part, to left and right ventricular precursors, respectively.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lineage tracing data.

claim: The two populations of Tbx5+ and Mef2cAHF+ labeled cells appeared largely mutually exclusive, except perhaps a narrow stripe of cells at the border between the forming left and right ventricles.
source: We performed simultaneously lineage tracing of Tbx5+ and Mef2cAHF + cells using separate reporters for Cre (RosamTmG) and Dre (RosanKmB) activity and found that the two populations of labeled cells appeared largely mutually exclusive, except perhaps a narrow stripe of cells at the border between the forming left and right ventricles (Figure 7N).
evidence: This is shown by dual lineage tracing in Figure 7N.

claim: A small population of Tbx5/Mef2cAHF double positive cells exists early in development.
source: We confirmed the existence of a small population of double positive cells early in development using the intersectional Cre/Dre reporter described previously.
evidence: This is shown by intersectional lineage tracing in Figure 7O-P.

claim: Labeling at E6.5 with the intersectional reporter marked a small population of cells that would eventually form a narrow ring of cells at the border between the left and right ventricles in the forming IVS.
source: Labeling at E6.5 marked a small population of cells that would eventually go on to form a narrow ring of cells at the border between the left and right ventricles in the forming IVS (Figure 7O–P and Figure 7—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This is shown by intersectional lineage tracing in Figure 7O-P and Figure 7—figure supplement 3D.

claim: A compartment boundary between the future left and right ventricles is established early, prior to cardiac morphogenesis.
source: In summary, genetic lineage labeling of the earlyTbx5+ and Mef2cAHF + precursors along with our clonal analysis of early Mesp1+ progenitors that contribute to the IVS suggest that a compartment boundary between the future left and right ventricles is established early, prior to cardiac morphogenesis
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lineage tracing and clonal analysis data.

claim: Early progenitors positive for both Tbx5 and Mef2cAHF will contribute specifically to the forming IVS.
source: and that early progenitors positive for both Tbx5 and Mef2cAHF will go on to contribute specifically to the forming IVS.
evidence: This is based on the intersectional lineage tracing data in Figure 7O-P.

claim: The findings pinpoint the existence of specified cardiac precursors in gastrulating mesoderm.
source: Our findings, summarized in Figure 8, pinpoint the existence of specified cardiac precursors in gastrulating mesoderm
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: The findings highlight an unanticipated early segregation of first and second heart field progenitors in their contribution to distinct chambers of the developing heart.
source: and also highlight an unanticipated early segregation of first and second heart field progenitors in their contribution to distinct chambers of the developing heart.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: The findings define the orderly progression of gene expression that parallels the commitment of nascent mesoderm to a cardiovascular fate.
source: Further, we define the orderly progression of gene expression that parallels the commitment of nascent mesoderm to a cardiovascular fate.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings shown in Figure 3.

claim: Mesoderm is rapidly specified at or before E6.0 to E7.5 into discrete fates that anticipate anatomical localization.
source: Our results show that mesoderm is rapidly specified at or before E6.0 to E7.5 into discrete fates that anticipate anatomical localization.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the clonal analysis data.

claim: A precursor that could contribute to all chambers of the heart could only exist prior to gastrulation, likely in the epiblast or shortly thereafter.
source: Our results, and those of Lescroart et al. (2014), suggest that such a precursor could only exist prior to gastrulation, likely in the epiblast or shortly thereafter
evidence: This is an inference based on the current results and comparison with other studies.

claim: Early mesoderm is rapidly patterned such that specific cells are shunted towards a unique path that assigns them to a specific cardiac compartment.
source: and that early mesoderm is rapidly patterned such that specific cells are shunted towards a unique path that assigns them to a specific cardiac compartment.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the clonal analysis data.

claim: The Smarcd3-expressing cardiac precursor population is already specified into separate populations that will contribute to the left ventricle and atria, as marked by Tbx5, and the right ventricle and outflow tract, as labeled by the Mef2cAHF enhancer.
source: The Smarcd3-expressing cardiac precursor population is already specified into separate populations that will contribute to the left ventricle and atria, as marked by Tbx5, and the right ventricle and outflow tract, as labeled by the Mef2cAHF enhancer.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lineage tracing data.

claim: Both left and right ventricular progenitors are independently established early in development and are separated by a compartment boundary.
source: we additionally show, at both a population and single cell level, that both left and right ventricular progenitors are independently established early in development and are separated by a compartment boundary.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the clonal analysis and lineage tracing data.

claim: The compartment boundary between left and right ventricles is derived from a unique population of early progenitors that express Tbx5 as well as a subpopulation of cells co-expressing the Mef2cAHF enhancer.
source: This compartment boundary is derived from a unique population of early progenitors that express Tbx5 as well as a subpopulation of cells co-expressing the Mef2cAHF enhancer
evidence: This is based on the intersectional lineage tracing data in Figure 7O-P.

claim: A relatively small number of cells may be important in establishing and/or maintaining the border between the left and right ventricles.
source: suggesting that a relatively small number of cells may be important in establishing and/or maintaining this border between the left and right ventricles.
evidence: This is an inference based on the intersectional lineage tracing data.

claim: In organisms with a simpler heart, such as zebrafish or Ciona, there is also a very early specification of cardiac precursors.
source: In organisms with a simpler heart, such as zebrafish or Ciona (Stolfi et al., 2010; Tolkin and Christiaen, 2012; Stainier et al., 1993; Keegan et al., 2004), there is also a very early specification of cardiac precursors.
evidence: This is based on citations to previous studies.

claim: Fate mapping in the chick embryo suggests distinct origins of the outflow tract vs the remainder of the heart, but does not indicate a compartmentalization of left and right ventricular progenitors, nor what molecular identity early cardiac precursors adopt.
source: Indeed, fate mapping in the chick embryo suggests distinct origins of the outflow tract vs the remainder of the heart, but does not indicate a compartmentalization of left and right ventricular progenitors, nor what molecular identity early cardiac precursors adopt (Camp et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on a citation to a previous study.

claim: The mouse embryo, despite the complexity of its developing heart, has a very early patterning and allocation of mesodermal cells to specific cardiac fates and anatomical derivatives.
source: Our data suggest that the mouse embryo, despite the complexity of its developing heart, has a very early patterning and allocation of mesodermal cells to specific cardiac fates and anatomical derivatives.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: It has been hypothesized that simpler organisms have integrated cardiac and pharyngeal mesoderm into a single lineage, the so-called cardiopharyngeal mesoderm.
source: In addition, it has been hypothesized that simpler organisms have integrated cardiac and pharyngeal mesoderm into a single lineage, the so-called cardiopharyngeal mesoderm (Stolfi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on a citation to a previous study.

claim: Retrospective clonal analysis in the mouse suggests a conservation of shared cardiac and pharyngeal lineages.
source: Retrospective clonal analysis in the mouse (Lescroart et al., 2010) suggests a conservation of shared cardiac and pharyngeal lineages
evidence: This is based on a citation to a previous study.

claim: Lescroart and colleagues reported rare instances of Mesp1+ clones co-labeling head muscles and the heart.
source: Lescroart and colleagues more recently reported rare instances of Mesp1+ clones co-labeling head muscles and the heart (Lescroart et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on a citation to a previous study.

claim: In the current lineage labeling experiments using the MADM system, there is no convincing evidence for a common heart and head muscle progenitor.
source: In our lineage labeling experiments, using the MADM system, we do not see convincing evidence for a common heart and head muscle progenitor.
evidence: This is based on the absence of such clones in the MADM data.

claim: Smarcd3+ precursors contribute to heart but not facial muscle.
source: Additionally, Smarcd3+ precursors contribute to heart but not facial muscle.
evidence: This is based on the lineage tracing data in Figure 5.

claim: The collective data do not support a common precursor for heart and facial muscle, but a rare population of common progenitors cannot be definitively ruled out.
source: While our collective data do not support a common precursor for heart and facial muscle, we cannot definitively rule out a rare population of common progenitors.
evidence: This is a cautious conclusion acknowledging the limitations of the data.

claim: On average, 1/3 of the total number of cells at E7.5 are Mesp1Cre-derived.
source: On average, 1/3 of the total number of cells are Mesp1Cre-derived.
evidence: This is shown by FACS analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: No cTNT positive cells were seen at E7.5 in Mesp1Cre embryos.
source: No cTNT positive cells were seen at this time point.
evidence: This is shown by FACS analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The Sox2::Cre line is active in epiblast cells at E6.5 with little or no activity in extraembryonic tissues when passed through the male germline.
source: The epiblast-specific Cre line, Sox2::Cre, is active in epiblast cells at E6.5 with little or no activity in extraembryonic tissues when passed through the male germline.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-B.
